symbols.name: real numerator
symbols.meaning: The integer multiplier of the real part of a grid value.
symbols.quote: The integer multiplier of its real part is $\sigma_1$, and of its imaginary part is $\sigma_2$.

symbols.name: imaginary numerator
symbols.meaning: The integer multiplier of the imaginary part of a grid value.
symbols.quote: The integer multiplier of its real part is $\sigma_1$, and of its imaginary part is $\sigma_2$.

symbols.name: product coefficient
symbols.meaning: The jth Gaussian integer coefficient of the product before normalization.
symbols.quote: Here $\Gamma_j$ is the $j$th output coefficient of the product, a Gaussian integer (the paper's $H_j$).

symbols.name: word width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in a signed two's-complement word, a count of bits.
symbols.quote: A signed two's-complement word of $\mu$ bits holds every integer from $-2^{\mu-1}$ to $2^{\mu-1}-1$, so $\mu=p+2$ bits hold each component.

symbols.name: truncation toward zero
symbols.meaning: The map that sends a real number to the integer nearest to it on the side of 0.
symbols.quote: $\mathrm{trunc}_0$ replaces a real number by the integer nearest to it on the side of $0$, so $\mathrm{trunc}_0(-2.7)=-2$.

relations.quote: A grid numerator is the numerator of a [Gaussian dyadic](gaussian-dyadics.md) with denominator $2^p$.
Each grid numerator is an input to [Carry propagation](carry-propagation.md), which converts integer coefficients into a binary string.
